plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control: limma-trend DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a gene-level TPM table from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 psoriasis-lesional vs 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch), with no raw counts or quantification directories delivered. Per the grounded procedure for TPM/FPKM input, DESeq2/edgeR/voom count models are inapplicable (they assume raw integer counts with NB variance); limma-trend on log2(TPM+1) is the correct model. The plan runs: (1) sample-structure QC on log2(TPM+1) via PCA/MDS and sample-distance heatmap to confirm the lesional/control split and flag outliers before any modeling decision is finalized; (2) low-abundance filtering at >=1 TPM in at least 6 samples (the smaller group size) followed by log2(TPM+1) transform only (no count-based size-factor/TMM normalization, since TPM already carries within-sample scaling); (3) an explicit-reference-level design (control as reference, contrast = lesional - control) fit with limma (lmFit + eBayes, trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE) and BH-adjusted topTable output; (4) fgsea preranked GSEA on the moderated t-statistic (the limma analog of the Wald statistic) against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome gene sets, both staged locally for human, with the standard 15-500 gene set size window and redundancy collapse; (5) a reproducibility-complete report naming the design, thresholds, gene counts, leading-edge genes, and package/collection versions. This directly answers 'which genes differ between lesional and control' with the assay-appropriate model given the TPM-only delivery, and adds pathway context without overclaiming beyond what the ranked-list method supports.
